preview: Interview experience of Jishnu Bandodkar from VJTI for the Trainee Software Engineer role at HSBC Technology India during the 2025 placement drive.
content: Name: Jishnu Bandodkar B.Tech Computer Engineering 2022-26 Company Details HSBC Technology India Role: Trainee Software Engineer Job Profile CTC: INR 15,03,097 lakhs per annum Cost to Company + 1.4 Lakhs On Target Variable Pay, subject to periodic internal reviews (Breakdown is not provided to us till now, for specific details check during your time.) Location: Pune/Bangalore/Hyderabad Criteria: CS/IT Branch only, CPI: 7 and above and 10-12th 70% and above Hi, I am Jishnu Bandodkar, a final year Computer Engineering student from VJTI. I am glad to share that I have secured a full time offer from HSBC Technology India for the role of Trainee Software Engineer and excited to share with you my interview experience. Key Note: I will be sharing all the details that I feel important for drives, please be free to read for any specific section you need. Overall Campus Drive Experience So I will start with a gist of overall experience from applying to very first company for internship which was JPMC (it is the only company which comes so early 😅) till my placement interview experience. JPMC usually comes around March End / April start in the second year (4th sem) for internship, and then other companies start coming from July start (like in mid summer vacation). So please start preparing accordingly. I was in a frame of mind that companies would start coming after the third year starts, and I would have sufficient time to prepare during my vacation, but in the second last week of June itself we received a notification that companies are coming from the first week of July itself. TPO usually tells you to register on Superset two-three weeks before April and please fill all your details properly for smooth registration during the campus drive. Ya, so, you wouldn’t find my interview experience for internship drive because I didn’t get any offer from any company for internship 😭 (Yes, you read that right). Our class strength is 90 (CS branch) and only 45-50 students got placed in the companies on campus for internships. Rest of them secured internships through their relative contacts, some through VJTI TBI, some through COE-CNDS labs, 2-3 (afaik) through hackathons (might be more, not sure though), while the rest (including me) did our internship under our FYP mentor. (FYP stands for final year project, you all will be told to do a project in team of 4 in your final year and assign a mentor(any one from our faculties) for that and under them you can do your internship, (more details you will get from your faculties at end of 6th sem)) Usually for OA, following things are asked: -> DSA (majorly asked by most of companies) -> Aptitude (Logical Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning, etc) (usually asked by finance companies, start-ups) -> CS fundamentals (for software roles) Topics included: OOPS, DBMS, SQL, OS, CN -> C++, Java, Python (isko alag se likha kyuki kuch companies agar ye languages pe majorly kaam karti hogi toh ispe jarur puchegi) -> If role is full stack engineer or related to web development, then HTML, CSS, Javascript, Java -> ML (agar Data Science / Data Engineering / AI/ML related kaam karni wali companies ho toh puchegi) -> Kabhi kabhi HR type questions bhi puch leti hai, HSBC mai hi pucha tha, aage padho for better details) This is a broader scope of majorly asked in OA. Some of the major platforms on which you might have to give your OA on are: Hackerrank, Hackkearth, SHL, IMocha, etc. For some, you might have to install their app. So make sure you are acquainted with the platform so that you can focus more on the questions during the test. DSA involves coding, while others are MCQ type. There was one session by Cantilever Labs about how your resume should look like, important tips during interviews, GD, etc.(guidance session regarding campus drive). Make sure to attend if such types of sessions are conducted during your time, because those experts perfectly know what the recruiters need. FTE Campus Experience This was an overview of my internship experience. I will now start with my full time campus experience. So, our full time drive started around mid July, just after the start of 7th sem. Now I had an experience of an entire year of internship campus drive, so first of all in my summer vacation I listed down all my weak points, my mistakes and what all things I need to improve for placements. This helped me to pass the OAs of Infosys, Clevertap, UPL, Fractal, HSBC and even Oracle as well. (internship ke time ek OA pass nhi kiya, placements me saare kiye 💪) So basically whichever company comes, first research about their interview experience (mostly on campus) on CoC archives, google, Leetcode Discuss. I even followed one of my senior’s youtube channel (see resources), for interview experience. Google pe toh mostly mil hi jaayega. Woh padh lena aur usme se find out the most asked topics by the company. (Maine toh ek google doc hi banaya tha which contained important topics of upcoming companies filtered out by myself.) Agar nhi mile toh company ke baare me research karo, find out what type of work does the company does and socho OA mai kya aa sakta.(You might need to do this for start ups). So here are the subjects you need to do for placements (in priority order): -> DSA (must, OA, interviews mai to puchte hi hai) -> CS fundamentals: DBMS + SQL (High priority) OOPS (High priority) OS, CN (Medium to low priority) System Design (Low priority, mostly HLD hi puchenge) -> Aptitude, Puzzles (Usually asked in OAs, sometimes in interviews) HSBC Interview Experience Now let me start with my HSBC Interview experience. We received mail from TPO on 13/08/2025 about the application. The entire next week was a heavy downpour in Mumbai due to which we didn’t attend the lectures. Also the upcoming week was Ganpati Vacations. So we almost had a 2 week holiday where we got sufficient time for preparation. But within that we had drives for UPL and Fractal too. The entire hiring process of HSBC was as follows: PPT(20/08/2025) -> Simulate test (20/08/2025) -> Codility test (20/08/2025) -> Technical Interview (02/09/2025) -> HR Interview (02/09/2025) 20/08/2025 PPT (3 pm - 4 pm) In PPT (Pre-Placement Talk), the recruiters give information about their company. Make sure to attend the PPT and make notes during the interview. Take screenshots of slides. Revise those before going to the interview. It helps you to answer HR questions like: Why do you want to join our company? What do you know about our company? Make sure to know about their current CEO, India branch CEO as such types of questions are asked in the interview. You can find information about the company from their LinkedIn, google, wikipedia and their website. Before the PPT, we were told to fill a registration form. They had mentioned to apply using our college mail id in the email, but I hurriedly filled the form first using my personal mail id and then read the email properly. Fortunately, I withdrew my application and reapplied using college mail id within the time limit, after informing the TPO CR. Make sure to read all the email properly because HSBC rejected those candidates (almost 30) who applied with their personal mail ids. Round 1: Simulate Test (4:30 pm - 5:40 pm) This round started just after our PPT got over, within 10-15 minutes. This was supposed to be a 70 minute round, but they didn’t set a time limit to the test and the test was lengthy, so most of the candidates’ test went on for 2 hours and above. Those who exceeded the time limit were rejected. So make sure that you complete the test on time. The test consisted of 30 HR type long situational questions and 37 aptitude questions. Out of 167 applicants, 100 proceeded for Codility round Round 2: Codility Test (7 pm - 8:40 pm) This test consisted of 3 DSA questions of easy-medium difficulty type. This round was 100 min. I completed all three questions with all test cases passed within 30 minutes. The three questions were: 1. Given a string containing only digits ‘6’ and ‘9’, replace at most one digit (6->9,9->6) to make the largest integer possible. For example: Input: num=”996996” Output=”999996” Code: string solve(string& num){ for(int i=0;i<num.size();i++){ if(num[i]=='6'){ num[i]='9'; break; } } return num; } 2. This was a video question. A robot moves around the X-Y plane and can only turn in four directions: North, South, East, West. The robot moves one unit in one move. Given a string moves consisting of only following characters: ^ for N, > for E, v for S and < for W, find out whether the robot completes a rectangle or not. Code: bool solve(string& moves){ unordered_map<char,pair<int,int>> mpp={ {'^',{-1,0}}, {'>',{0,1}}, {'v',{1,0}}, {'<',{0,-1}}, }; vector<pair<int,int>> path; int x=0,y=0; for(char c:moves){ x+=mpp[c].first; y+=mpp[c].second; path.push_back({x,y}); } if(x!=0 || y!=0) return false; int minx=INT_MAX,maxx=INT_MIN,miny=INT_MAX,maxy=INT_MIN; for(auto [x,y]:path){ minx=min(minx,x); maxx=max(maxx,x); miny=min(miny,y); maxy=max(maxy,y); } if(2*(maxx-minx+maxy-miny)!=moves.size()) return false; for(auto [x,y]:path){ if(!((x==minx || x==maxx) && (y==miny || y==maxy))) return false; } return true; } 3. You are given a grid consisted of ‘*’ (Land) and ‘.’ (Water). There are three types of islands: one of one block, another of 2 blocks and the third of three blocks. You have to find how many blocks of each type are present. Code: vector<pair<int,int>> dir={{0,1},{0,-1},{1,0},{-1,0}}; int dfs(int i, int j, vector<vector<bool>>& vis, vector<string>& grid){ int m=grid.size(),n=grid[0].size(); int cnt=1; vis[i][j]=true; for(auto [di,dj]:dir){ int ni=i+di,nj=j+dj; if(ni>=0 && ni<m && nj>=0 && nj<n && grid[ni][nj]=='*' && !vis[ni][nj]) cnt+=dfs(ni,nj,vis,grid); } return cnt; } vector<int> solve(vector<string>& grid){ int m=grid.size(),n=grid[0].size(); vector<vector<bool>> vis(m,vector<bool>(n,false)); vector<int> ans(3,0); for(int i=0;i<m;i++){ for(int j=0;j<n;j++){ if(grid[i][j]=='*' && !vis[i][j]){ int sz=dfs(i,j,vis,grid); if(sz==1) ans[0]++; else if(sz==2) ans[1]++; else if(sz==3) ans[2]++; } } } return ans; } Shortlists for Interviews were declared on 29/08/2025. Actually on this day I had my virtual interviews for Fractal AI, in which I gave all the three rounds (two technical + 1 HR, so I was hoping to get selected for Fractal, but still they didn’t select me 😭. But as it is said, something better was waiting for me 🤩). On the same day, we received a candidature form to be filled handwritten and we had to upload the form and our latest resume by next day 11:00 am (we received the shortlist at night 10 pm 🥲). Interviews (02/09/2025) We had our interviews from college but the interviews were virtual. Technical interviews would start at 9:30 am and HR at 2:30 pm. The night before, we were told to sign up on the JDoodle website, which we could use for coding solutions. We were asked to assemble at college by 8:30 am. 40 students were selected. There were 5 panelists. 5 groups of 8 students were made by sorting in alphabetical order of our initial names. One student from each group was called and were interviewed simultaneously by 5 different interviewers. (One-one interview). Round 3: Technical Interview (10:20 am - 11:10 am) Now this time differed for each group. I was in group 3 and each interview from our group lasted at least 40-45 mins. (sirf mera aur mere dost ka 1 hr chala 😅). On the contrary, other group’s interviews were being done in 25-30 mins. Each interviewer has a different mentality and different type of accessing the candidate. That’s why some of my friends were just asked simple questions on C++, OOPs and coding questions and were sent, whereas I had a long and deep conversation with the interviewer. So always be ready for any kind of situation. Still always ask those candidates questions whose interviews are already done as type of questions get repeated. (Tip for those who have a virtual interview: Always join 5-10 mins before the predecided time. Because if you have a less time limit interview, like I had for Fractal (only 15 mins each round), and if the interviewer also joins early, you get some extra time to interact with the interviewer and impress him/her more). My interview: The interviewer joined and told me to wait for a while. After 2-3 minutes he started his camera. He introduced himself and allowed me to introduce myself. Always have an introduction ready as this is a definite question asked in every round. Your introduction should include the following points: -> Your name, year, branch, (CPI: only if > 9) -> Domain of expertise (for me it was full stack development) -> Your internship experience in short (i didn’t include it because i did it under my fyp guide, so thodi sharm aa rhi thi mujhe 😅) -> any hackathon experience (mostly include industry level hackathons if any) -> any leadership experience / club experience (like work did in CoC, Enthu, etc) -> any significant achievements worth mentioning (like kisi competition / hackathon mai kuch prize mila ho) Your introduction is a pathway / guide for your further interview. Most of the time, the interviewer starts asking questions based on your introduction itself. He started with, “Explain to me your hackathon project.” Always use the STAR method to explain your projects. (One trick joh maine use ki thi: apna pura project explanation + your role / contribution in that - chatgpt ko daaldo aur bolo ki STAR format mai explain karke de, then from its response curate it according to your style. Gpt bohot hi hard english mai dega, usko conversational tone mai tumhe khud banana hoga). After that he asked me about my role and I explained to him thoroughly, the tech stack I used, why I selected that tech stack in detail). Always know the whys of everything you implemented and used in your project. He seemed satisfied with my response because he told me that since you explained it so beautifully I don’t have any further questions. This moment really boosted my morale for the further part of the interview. He had my resume opened on his side and was going through my resume. He literally viewed my Leetcode Profile which I had put in my resume. He was really impressed with my consistency and number of questions solved, which further fueled my confidence. Then he enquired about my FYP project and about its advancements. Next he asked whether I was born and brought up in Mumbai, and what about Mumbai do you like the most. I answered about Mumbai’s better commute and other facilities as compared to villages, moreover in Mumbai you get the credit for your hardwork. Then he asked, 'What will you do to solve the congestion problem in Mumbai?' I gave a few suggestions, like analysing the routes where more vehicles commute throughout the day and place a traffic police there, increase the time limit of green signal on main roads like S.V Road, etc. But he said he wanted something out of the box, related to software development. I gave a few suggestions like, attracting more people to use public transport, marketing apps like Yatri, Chalo, m-indicator, etc. I realised that whatever I suggested was already implemented, so I took a pause for a while. Then he gave a hint like suppose I want to use the public transport to go from my home to office, then what shall you do to ease my journey. That clicked with me of one idea like, we could fix a vehicle which could pick and drop a group of people from their source to destination. He then told me that since time was running out, and he wanted to test my coding skills, let’s go towards DSA. He then gave me the following coding problem: Q: Given a string containing only digits (‘0’ to ‘9’), find out the maximum number by converting the substring made by concatenating two adjacent characters into a number. Example: num=”5051554” output: 55 Code: int solve(string& num){ int ans=0; for(int i=0;i<num.size()-1;i++){ string temp=""; temp.push_back(num[i]); temp.push_back(num[i+1]); ans=max(ans,stoi(temp)); } return ans; } TC: O(n) SC: O(1) I explained the solution along with its time and space complexity. Make sure to first explain the solution and then code up and at the end explain the time and space complexity. He then asked the usual question: Why do you want to join HSBC? (This question is usually asked by most of the companies and make sure to prepare your answer for this. While answering this make sure to include how you can create an impact by joining the company, because usually that is what interviewers see). At the end, he asked me whether I had any questions for him. Always ask the interviewer 1-2 questions because it is the final chance to set your impression on him. I asked the following question: “In which department do you work in?” (Do not ask this if the interviewer has already mentioned it in his/her intro). Then I asked one more question, “How does your team adapt to changes in technology and implement those changes within the projects?”. He was really impressed by this question. I do not recall what he answered but he mentioned something about focusing on the need to understand the problem and in which part the change is required. With this my technical interview ended. It lasted about 1 hr. But you don’t even feel how the time passes when you are interacting with a good interviewer. There was no point where I felt nervous or under pressure. Since I came out of the room around 11:30 am and the HR round was scheduled to be after 2:30 pm, I had sufficient time to prepare. I then met my friends, shared my experience and had my lunch (since I was very hungry 😂 after talking so much). We expected the technical round to be over around 1:30 - 2. But it got delayed, because our’s and most of group 1 candidates had their first round around 40-50 minutes. In the meantime I was preparing for typical HR questions (resources below). The first round almost went up to 3-3:30pm. We all were literally bored till then. I had a quick nap after I felt that my preparation was enough (I didn’t read all the questions mentioned in the resource, but I made a quick structure of any question that would come up to me. Usually HR questions are also to be answered in STAR format, and your answers should be linked to any experience that you might have while participating in hackathons, competitions, working for clubs, etc. Try to answer most of your questions using situations that you have really experienced, do not try to bluff, because usually HR is taken by senior personnel so they might catch you bluffing. But sometimes while studying for HR, you might see questions which you haven’t experienced at all, so for such questions, try to answer them by taking references from nearby or similar situations experienced by you. Round 3: HR round (6 pm - 6:15 pm) My group (group 3) were waiting for results till 5:55 pm. All other groups had their HR done before us. (Basically they were taking groups in order how their technical round was finished in order - like HR round happened in following order: Group 2 -> 4 -> 5 -> 1 -> 3) The interviewer was the same guy who took our PPT. He was the hiring lead of HSBC. He started with his introduction and told me to introduce myself. He then asked whether I was recruited by some company during the internship drive. I replied no. He then asked what was the problem and why weren’t you selected by any company. I gave the reason and explained how I worked on improving myself making sure that I get selected for full time campus drive. Then he asked me about my internship project, the problems faced by me and how I solved it. I gave a detailed explanation for that. After that he asked if I had any questions for him. I asked the following question: “What type of projects are freshers assigned? And what are the things that a fresher should keep in mind while joining HSBC?” With that my interview ended. I felt pretty confident leaving the room because I didn’t fumble nor did I take a long pause for any question asked to me. We were informed that the results would be announced at the end of the day on whatsapp. The results came around 10:15 pm. HSBC selected around 13 candidates for full time and 4 for interns. I was happy to be one of them. I literally felt a sigh of relief that all my preparations were worth it and had got their fruit of success. Tips / Points to keep in mind -> Always keep your answers ready for the following questions: 1. Introduce yourself (Asked at the beginning of every interview) 2. Introduce yourself without technical terms / which is not present in your resume (Usually talk about your hobbies, interests, aspirations, etc) (usually asked in HR) 3. STAR format for at least top 2 projects that you keep in your resume + for internship project. (if you put your internship project then they will ask about that, else if you have done any project during hackathon or in a team they will ask about that) 4. Why do you want to join our company? 5. Why should we hire you? 6. What are your strengths and weaknesses? -> Know your resume very well, especially the project that you keep on top. Also if the company is using a particular language or tech stack and if that is present in your resume, then they will grill you on that (for example, most of the banks / companies, java is used. Also, companies working on quants (Dolat Capital) uses C++ primarily. So be prepared for questions in depth on that.) -> Always keep your resume upto one page. Remove all those things which are not relevant. TPO usually provides the format for resume, but if you want the format I used, it is this: Jake's Resume - Overleaf, Online LaTeX Editor -> It’s important to focus only on the skills and technologies you’re truly comfortable with. Include only those in your resume. Don’t forget to seek feedback from seniors to make improvements, and try to increase your ATS score to enhance your chances of getting shortlisted. -> Always bold out the points within your resume, on which you want to invite questions on. Make sure to include those keywords present in the job description of the company (JD). -> Do not try to bluff about the things that you haven’t done or experienced. Interviewers can easily judge if you try to do that. -> Make sure to practice core computer science concepts like DSA, OOPS, and DBMS regularly. Companies may begin their recruitment process during vacations, so being consistently prepared will give you an advantage. Also, stay on top of CS fundamentals to ensure you’re ready when the opportunity arises. -> Practice important DSA topics well in advance. While solving DSA questions, have a time bound and speak up your approach like you are talking to an interviewer. Refer 30-40 important questions list on GFG/Interview Bit for OS, DBMS, OOPS. ChatGPT can be very helpful for solving doubts and explaining key concepts. -> During interviews, it’s essential to communicate your thought process clearly. Speaking out loud while solving problems not only helps interviewers follow your logic but also gives them the opportunity to provide hints if you're heading in the wrong direction. It’s equally important to mention edge cases during problem-solving, as it shows your thorough approach to tackling challenges. -> While technical skills are a must, how you express them matters just as much. When you’re unsure or nervous, take a deep breath, and don’t hesitate to ask the interviewer for clarification. It demonstrates that you’re thinking critically before answering, rather than rushing. Body language is important, so have an upright, confident posture during the interview. -> Technical aspects you have to prepare, no doubt about that. But make sure you prepare on your communication skills and there’s only one way to do it and it's practice. Talk to people, strangers, your teachers, higher authorities, take any opportunity of public speaking. -> For virtual interviews, make sure you sit in a quiet place with no disturbance and have a stable internet connection throughout the day. Make sure your camera is on but blur off the background as only your face is important during interviews. -> Usually for virtual interviews, you get to know the name of the interviewer a day before. Search on LinkedIn what tech stack does he/she use, what is he/she proficient in and based on that try to gauge the questions that might be asked in the interview. -> Usually technical rounds are taken by senior engineers themselves or project managers. HR round is taken by HR / Director / VP. So create two types of questions to be asked at the end of the interview. -> At CoC, we have mock interviews conducted by seniors, which were incredibly helpful for practicing and receiving constructive feedback before facing the real deal. These mock sessions gave me a chance to refine my skills in a more relaxed environment. -> Lastly, reading through other candidates’ interview experiences can provide valuable insights, as interview formats are often similar across companies. This will help you better understand what to expect and how to approach different interview stages. -> This were some of the points that I read from CoC archives, which I found important: Resources DSA: Strivers A2Z DSA Course/Sheet - Crack Any FAANG or PBCs For DSA, fix a language (either C++ / Java / Python) and then practice in that language itself. I followed the Striver’s sheet, however you may use any sheet of your choice, but just stick to that till the end. For those candidates who just want to do DSA for interview preparation, just doing Leetcode is fine. But stay consistent on Leetcode, give contests, solve POTDs so that while revising you can focus on other topics. If you are into CP, then you might use CodeChef, Codeforces, etc. OOPS: OOPS Sheet DBMS: DBMS Sheet SQL: SQL 50 - Study Plan - LeetCode Solve SQL | HackerRank OS: OS Sheet CN: CN Sheet Language Oriented: Refer InterviewBit / GFG top questions Aptitude: IndiaBIX Aptitude YT Playlist System Design: Gaurav Sen YT Playlist LLD Playlist HR: Top HR Interview Questions and Answers: Freshers & Experienced (2025) - InterviewBit Puzzles: Top 100 Puzzles Asked In Interviews - GeeksforGeeks Resume template: Jake's Resume - Overleaf, Online LaTeX Editor Meet Ranka Youtube Channel: Meet Ranka - YouTube With this I will end my interview experience. I hope it was fun reading and might have helped in your interview preparation. You can reach out to me here: Jishnu Bandodkar
